2608.03921.title: The Transformer Revolution, Part 1: Dynamic Processing through Output- Weight Interconnections
2608.03921.paper_summary: This paper offers a new interpretation of the Transformer during inference. Against the "stochastic parrot" view that large language models merely reproduce statistical regularities learned in training, we argue that Transformers construct and apply prompt-dependent transformations whose parameters are generated during inference. We call this form of computation SIDPP: Sequence-level Interactive Dynamic Parallel Processing. The Transformer is interpreted as a system that transforms concepts by means of concepts. Token vectors are the concepts to be transformed; parameterized transformations defined by matrices and vectors are the transforming concepts. These may be static, when fixed through training, or dynamic, when generated from the input sequence. Mechanically, they correspond to groups of simple neural networks. The Transformer's architectural novelty lies in output-weight interconnections, through which the outputs of some networks determine the weights of others, alongside ordinary output-input interconnections. By means of these interconnections, the system constructs transformations from the prompt and uses them to modify token representations. The contribution of dynamic processing grows with prompt length and may equal or exceed that of static processing, a phenomenon we call strong prompt sensitivity. This account bears on interpretability, predictability, control, and the design of smaller, more sustainable systems. Finally, since the human neural system possesses the mechanisms required to implement SIDPP, we argue that a form of SIDPP may, in principle, be neurally realized in the cerebral cortex. We therefore conjecture that human language processing may itself be a form of SIDPP produced by a functional architecture relevantly similar to that of the Transformer.
2608.03921.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文提供了對於推理過程中 Transformer 的新詮釋。針對「隨機鸚鵡」的觀點，即大型語言模型僅僅重現訓練中學到的統計規律，我們主張 Transformer 構建並應用依賴於提示的轉換，其參數在推理過程中生成。我們稱這種計算形式為 SIDPP：序列級互動動態並行處理。Transformer 被解釋為一個通過概念來轉換概念的系統。標記向量是要被轉換的概念；由矩陣和向量定義的參數化轉換是轉換的概念。這些轉換可以是靜態的，當它們在訓練中被固定時，或者是動態的，當它們從輸入序列中生成時。在機械上，它們對應於一組簡單的神經網絡。Transformer 的架構新穎之處在於輸出權重互連，通過這些互連，一些網絡的輸出決定其他網絡的權重，還有普通的輸出-輸入互連。藉助這些互連，系統從提示中構建轉換並用它們來修改標記表示。動態處理的貢獻隨著提示長度的增加而增長，並可能等於或超過靜態處理的貢獻，這一現象我們稱之為強提示敏感性。這一解釋與可解釋性、可預測性、控制以及設計更小、更可持續的系統相關。最後，由於人類神經系統擁有實現 SIDPP 所需的機制，我們主張在原則上，SIDPP 的一種形式可以在大腦皮層中神經實現。因此，我們推測人類語言處理本身可能是一種由與 Transformer 的功能架構相關相似的形式所產生的 SIDPP。
